item.title: Day 2: Profit-Taking Pulls TTF Off €65 High — But €50 Holds
item.description: Day 3 of Hormuz with no diplomatic off-ramp: TTF pulled back to €53 from Monday's €65 panic spike, but the 30% storage floor just broke. The council validated 16 trade ideas out of 21 — the JKM-TTF parity spread and cheap Apr €65 calls stand out as the highest-conviction asymmetric plays. The refill math at €53+ TTF is brutal; this summer will test every assumption.

item.title: TTF Prints €14 Intraday Range — Biggest Single-Session Swing Since 2022 Energy Crisis
item.description: Qatar's Ras Laffan shutdown transforms Hormuz from tail risk to live crisis — TTF's €14 intraday range signals a market groping for equilibrium between insurance-driven supply panic and coal-gas switching ceilings. With storage at 30% and a vortex split extending heating demand into March, the council validated 16 of 21 trade ideas, culling 5 duplicates and contradictions. Duration of the Qatar shutdown is the single variable separating a spike-and-fade from a 2022 redux.

item.title: Hormuz Shutdown Rewrites the Board — TTF & JKM Set for Monster Gap Higher at Monday Open
item.description: Hormuz rewrites everything: Iran's de facto closure of the world's most critical LNG chokepoint collides with EU storage at a historic 29.98% — the most acute gas risk environment since 2022. The council validated 13 of 21 trade ideas, culling 8 for duplicates, mispriced strikes, and internal contradictions. Duration of the Hormuz disruption is the single variable that separates a spike-and-fade from a regime change.

item.title: HH Crashes Through $3.00 to $2.92 — Storm Fern Rally Fully Erased; TTF Settles €30.90
item.description: Winter's last gasp meets structural fragility: HH crashes through $3 as US supply overwhelms, but EU storage at decade-lows and a fractured sanctions regime set up a volatile refill season. The transatlantic divergence — US surplus vs EU deficit — is this week's defining tension, and the council validated 14 of 21 trade ideas after culling 7 for redundancy and contradiction.

item.title: HH Bounces Off 5-Month Low at $2.86 — TTF Holds €31.50 as Regas Margins Turn Positive
item.description: The warm reprieve is a mirage. Storage at 30% with the Russian LNG ban activating in five weeks means the refill math is brutal — and a stratospheric vortex disruption could extend winter demand just as the market prices spring. Asymmetry favours upside protection.

item.title: HH Slides to $3.17 on Warmer Shift — TTF Drifts Lower to €31.25; NBP Mar Jumps 7%
item.description: EU storage at historic lows meets record LNG arrivals and fracturing sanctions unity — the market is pricing a comfortable spring while sitting on the thinnest cushion since 2022. The council validated 15 of 21 trade ideas, flagging dangerous concentration in long-Europe positions. Watch Thursday's EIA print and GIE weekly for the next directional catalyst.

item.title: TTF Eases to €32 After Iran Whipsaw — HH Eyes Gap Higher on Bomb Cyclone
item.description: Hormuz tensions collide with EU storage at historic lows — the gas market is caught between record LNG arrivals and a geopolitical tinderbox. The 30.8% storage level and Alpine hydro deficit make this week's data releases critical inflection points for Q2 positioning.
